entries.page: When to Molt; Feed and Program by Day
entries.notes: Optimum molt age about 65 (early) to 75 (late) weeks, decided on feed cost, egg prices, pullet cost and flock performance. Non-fasting molt: 7 days before, 16 h light then 24 h for 4 days, fine CaCO3, no added salt. Molt diet (high fibre, low energy, no added sodium, sodium max 0.035%) about 54-64 g per bird per day for up to ~84 days at 6-8 h light and 27-28 C. Days 18-19 switch to layer diet with mixed fine and coarse CaCO3, 64-73 g per day; days 20-21 full feed, 16 h light. Drinking water sodium 100 ppm or more harms results.

entries.page: Body Weight Target; Recovery Timeline; Post-Molt Production
entries.notes: Target: reduce to about the 18-week body weight (about 23% loss); brown hens must not lose more than 23%. Weigh twice weekly. Egg production must stop completely for at least 2 weeks. After re-stimulation (return to 15-16 h light): hen-day near 0% at +1 wk, about 76-79% at +5 wk, peak about 86-88% at +11 to +12 wk, about 76-79% at +40 wk. Post-molt feed about 64-95 g per day at +1 wk rising to 104-114 g at +40 wk. Molting after about 75 weeks lowers post-molt performance. This is a non-fasting programme; the farm's own day-by-day feed schedule is stored in the app separately.
